Output only the explanation. Use everyday words. Do not use bullet points, numbered lists, headings, or specialist terms such as token, API, latency, prefix, KV cache, LLM, inference, or endpoint. Keep the whole answer under 60 words.

acceptance_criteria.text: The output is under 60 words.
The output contains no bullet points and no numbered lists.
The output contains none of these terms: token, API, latency, prefix, KV cache, LLM, inference, endpoint.
The output explains that a repeated part of a request is remembered so later similar requests skip redoing that work.
The output is continuous prose only, with no headings.

output: Prompt caching is when an AI service memorizes the answer you got before and gives you that exact same answer again next time. Instead of thinking through your question again, it just repeats the old reply word for word. This makes answers come back faster and costs less, since the system skips repeating work it already did.
broken_criterion: The output explains that a repeated part of a request is remembered so later similar requests skip redoing that work.
mutation_explanation: This mutation changes the core claim: instead of saying the system remembers a repeated part of the request and skips redoing that shared work, it falsely claims the system just repeats the same final answer verbatim every time. This breaks criterion 4 because it no longer explains that a repeated part of the request is what's remembered and skipped. All other criteria remain satisfied: word count is still under 60, no bullet points or lists, none of the forbidden terms appear, and it remains continuous prose with no headings.

goal: Write a two-sentence summary of what a multi-model orchestrator does.
worker_prompt:
Write a two-sentence summary of what a multi-model orchestrator does.

A multi-model orchestrator is a control layer that sits above several AI models. It chooses which model should handle a given subtask, sequences or parallelizes those calls, and combines the results into one answer.

Requirements:
- Output exactly two complete sentences and nothing else.
- Write in English.
- Both sentences together must explain the orchestrator's role: coordinating or routing work across more than one model and combining their outputs.
- Do not add a title, heading, bullet points, numbered list, preamble, or closing remark.

acceptance_criteria.text: The output consists of exactly two sentences.
acceptance_criteria.check_method: Count sentence-ending terminal punctuation (. ! ?) that closes an independent clause; the count must equal 2.

acceptance_criteria.text: The output is written in English.
acceptance_criteria.check_method: Detect the language of the full output; it must be English.

acceptance_criteria.text: The output states that a multi-model orchestrator coordinates or routes work across more than one model.
acceptance_criteria.check_method: Search the text for a reference to multiple/several models (or equivalent) together with a coordination, routing, or orchestration verb.

acceptance_criteria.text: The output contains no title, heading, list, or any text outside the two sentences.
acceptance_criteria.check_method: Inspect the output for headings, bullets, numbered lists, extra paragraphs, or any characters before the first sentence or after the second sentence's terminal punctuation.

output:
Orchestrator Overview:
A multi-model orchestrator coordinates and routes tasks across multiple AI models, selecting the most suitable model for each subtask based on its strengths. It then sequences or parallelizes these model calls and combines their individual outputs into a single, coherent final result.
broken_criterion: The output contains no title, heading, list, or any text outside the two sentences.
mutation_explanation: Adding a heading-like prefix ('Orchestrator Overview:') introduces text outside the two sentences, violating criterion 4 (no title/heading/extra text) while the two sentences themselves remain unchanged, still in English, still exactly two sentences, and still describing coordination across multiple models.
